problem.statement: Count connected groups of 1s in a 2D grid using 4-direction adjacency.

grid.meaning: The input 2D grid whose 1 cells represent land and whose 0 cells represent non-land or already marked cells.

r.meaning: The current row index being scanned or explored.

c.meaning: The current column index being scanned or explored.

count.meaning: The number of connected land components whose exploration has been initiated.

stack.meaning: The collection of discovered land-cell coordinates awaiting neighbor expansion.

representation_requirements.description: Represent grid coordinates in a deterministic row-and-column scan with the current cell identified.
Represent only the side-sharing neighbors above, below, left, and right of the current cell.
Represent an unmarked 1 cell as the seed that starts one component exploration.
Represent discovered land cells as marked in grid so they cannot start or join another exploration.
Represent discovered but not yet expanded land-cell coordinates in stack.
Represent count increasing once for each newly discovered component seed.
Represent count after every grid cell has been scanned and every discovered component has been fully expanded.

semantic_invariants.statement: An adjacent cell is eligible only when it shares a side with the current cell: (r-1,c), (r+1,c), (r,c-1), or (r,c+1).
count increases exactly when the scan encounters a grid cell whose current value is 1 and which has not already been marked.
A land cell is changed from 1 to 0 when it is added to stack, so it cannot be added again.
Every coordinate in stack belongs to the same connected component as the seed currently being explored.
count equals the number of distinct connected components whose seeds have been encountered and whose flood-fill explorations have been initiated.
After the scan completes, every original 1 cell has been marked 0 and belongs to exactly one counted component.

completion_evidence.description: Identifies side-sharing neighbors and excludes diagonal adjacency.
Tracks the grid scan and identifies when an unmarked 1 cell starts a new component.
Tracks stack and grid as one component is expanded through eligible neighbors.
Preserves the order of marking a discovered land cell before adding it to stack.
Distinguishes starting a component from expanding cells already belonging to it.
Verifies count after all rows and columns have been processed.

terminal_behavior: Scan every row and column in deterministic order.
When grid[r][c] is 1, increment count, mark the seed cell as 0, and add its coordinate to stack.
While stack is nonempty, expand each coordinate through its four in-bounds side-sharing neighbors; mark and add each neighbor whose current value is 1.
After stack becomes empty, continue the grid scan for another unmarked 1 cell.
After all grid cells are scanned, return count.
